narrative:
The model predicts you have a 36% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help you graduate.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is your history of three past class failures. While students who passed had zero previous failures on average, your record of repeated setbacks strongly pushes the model toward expecting you will fail again.

The second most important factor is that you are receiving extra educational support at school. This actually works in your favor and pulls the prediction toward passing, because the model has learned that students getting this kind of targeted help tend to improve their chances.

Third, having your father as guardian also nudges the outcome slightly toward passing compared with the typical student who has their mother as guardian.

Even though the extra school support and your guardian are helping, they are not enough to overcome the heavy negative influence of your past failures. To improve, you should treat the remedial courses as a real opportunity: attend every session, ask for specific help on topics that caused your earlier failures, and build consistent daily study habits. Turning around your pattern of past setbacks is the single most important thing you can do to raise your chances of passing.
